h: Beatrix Potter Country on the Doorstep
p: Grizedale sits slap bang in Beatrix Potter country, which makes it easy to mix a high-energy morning with a gentler afternoon. Hill Top, her farmhouse at Near Sawrey, is now cared for by the National Trust and is just a short drive away. In Hawkshead, the Beatrix Potter Gallery shows her original illustrations in a little building in the village, and the cobbled streets are full of cafés and gift shops.

Over towards Coniston, Tarn Hows is a famously pretty spot with an easy path around the water, ideal for anyone whose legs are still shaking from the zips. On the eastern shore of Coniston Water, Brantwood, once the home of the Victorian thinker John Ruskin, has gardens with fantastic views across the lake to the Old Man of Coniston.

Practicalities matter in the Lakes. Mobile signal can be patchy in the forest, so screenshot your booking before you set off. The course takes a couple of hours, and the roads in and out can be slow, especially in the summer holidays, so don't book anything too tight afterwards.
Pack waterproofs even if the sky looks clear, because Lakeland weather changes its mind quickly. A dry pair of socks and a warm jumper waiting in the car can turn a soggy finish into a happy one.
